summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and epigastric abdominal pain following a medication error in which she mistakenly took fluconazole instead of prednisone. This led to under-treatment of her chronic graft-versus-host disease, requiring re-initiation of high-dose prednisone. The increase in steroids likely worsened steroid-induced gastritis, causing her symptoms. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed no acute pathology. She was treated with increased pantoprazole and initiation of sucralfate, with symptom improvement. Her transaminitis remained at baseline and was attributed to GVHD. Chronic hip pain was managed with oxycodone. Medication reconciliation was completed with patient and family education. She stabilized and was discharged home with updated medication instructions and follow-up plans.
